STANCE 31 - Treat redundant calling as a context-rot problem: measure attention mass over prior tool observations before blaming policy.

Mechanism. A tool result is just tokens in the prefix. If the trajectory has grown long, or if the observation was serialized in a format the model rarely saw during post-training (deeply nested JSON, escaped strings), the effective retrievability of that result degrades even though it is nominally in context. The policy then genuinely does not "already know" the answer at the moment of the second call; it is re-deriving from a prefix it cannot read. This predicts redundancy should rise monotonically with the token distance between the first result and the second call site.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: unnecessary-call rate rises with the token gap between the original observation and the redundant call, with the rate in the top distance quartile at least 2x the bottom quartile. Falsified if the rate is flat across distance quartiles, which would mean the result is equally ignored when it is three tokens away, and the defect is a policy habit rather than a retrieval failure.

Metrics. Per-call: token distance to the most recent matching observation, observation serialization format, trajectory length at call time, and whether the call was redundant. Aggregate: UCR by distance quartile, UCR by serialization format, and a needle-style retrieval probe score at matched context lengths as a capability control.

Controlled experiment. Replay logged trajectories against the frozen checkpoint twice: once verbatim, once with the prior observation re-injected immediately before the decision point in a compact canonical form. Same seeds, same decode config, paired by trajectory id. Only the position and format of the observation differ, so any UCR delta is attributable to retrievability.

Confounders. Re-injection also shortens effective distance and changes token counts, so it perturbs two variables at once unless a padding control arm is run. Long trajectories are also harder tasks, so distance correlates with difficulty. Prefix caching may make the two arms differ in latency, which can leak into any human-rated comparison.

Evidence and rollback. Report UCR by distance quartile, the re-injection arm delta, and the retrieval probe scores as MEASURED, naming the replay window and checkpoint hash. The 2x quartile ratio is an ESTIMATE chosen in advance as the effect size that would justify a context-engineering fix over a training fix; it is not read off prior data. Roll back re-injection if it raises prompt tokens per task by more than 10% (ESTIMATE budget) without a proportional UCR drop, because then it is trading spend for cosmetics.
risks: Source treats the prior tool result as reliably available in context without checking whether it is still retrievable at that distance.
No serialization-format control, so a formatting-induced retrieval failure would be misdiagnosed as a policy defect.
evidence_required: UCR by token-distance quartile between the prior observation and the redundant call, from a named replay window.
Paired verbatim versus re-injected-observation replay deltas plus needle-retrieval probe scores at matched context lengths.

STANCE 32 - Contrarian: the calculator is the wrong abstraction; the fix is to make the tool return a proof the model can cite instead of a bare number.

Mechanism. A bare numeric observation gives the policy nothing to condition on except trust. When the model re-calls, it is often because it cannot distinguish "I computed this" from "a tool told me this" in a prefix that renders both as plain text. Returning a structured result carrying the normalized expression, the value, and a call id gives the policy a citable handle, so the natural continuation becomes referencing the prior result rather than re-invoking. This is a tool-contract change, not a capability change.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: replacing bare numeric returns with structured cited results reduces UCR by at least 25% relative with no accuracy regression beyond noise. Falsified if UCR moves less than 5% relative, which would show the policy never attended to result provenance and the redundancy is independent of observation format.

Metrics. UCR, citation rate (fraction of final answers that reference a prior call id), accuracy on the tool-required stratum, mean calls per task, and observation token cost, since structured results are strictly larger. Guardrail: fabricated-citation rate, meaning answers referencing call ids that do not exist in the trajectory.

Controlled experiment. Two serving arms behind identical routing: bare-return and structured-return. Same frozen checkpoint, same eval set, same decode settings, traffic split by hash of task id so assignment is stable and balanced. No weights change in either arm, which is what isolates the tool contract as the only manipulated variable.

Confounders. Structured returns lengthen the prefix and therefore interact with the context-distance effect. Fabricated citations can inflate the citation rate while the underlying behavior is unchanged. If the parser is lenient, some structured returns may silently degrade to bare text and contaminate the arm.

Evidence and rollback. UCR, citation rate, fabricated-citation rate and accuracy must be MEASURED per arm with the eval-set id, checkpoint hash and parser version recorded. The 25% acceptance and 5% falsification bands are ESTIMATE, pre-registered as the smallest effect that would justify a tool-contract migration across all callers. Abort the structured arm immediately if fabricated-citation rate exceeds 1% absolute (ESTIMATE gate), because a plausible false citation is worse operationally than a redundant call.
risks: Source assumes a bare numeric observation carries provenance the policy can condition on, which it does not.
A citation mechanism can be gamed by fabricated call ids, producing plausible but unverifiable answers.
evidence_required: Per-arm UCR, citation rate and fabricated-citation rate for bare versus structured tool returns, with parser version.
Stratified accuracy and observation token cost per arm with the eval-set id and checkpoint hash.

corrected_answer:
STANCE 33 - Budget the agent explicitly: an enforced per-task call budget converts an open-ended behavior into a bounded, auditable one.

Mechanism. Redundant calling is unbounded because nothing in the loop bounds it. An orchestrator-side budget that admits at most K tool calls per task and returns a structured budget-exhausted observation forces the policy into the answer-now branch deterministically. This does not teach the model anything; it caps the tail. The mechanism is admission control, and its boundary condition is that K must exceed the genuine call depth of the hardest legitimate task or it will truncate correct work.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: there exists a K at which p99 calls per task falls by at least 40% while accuracy on the tool-required stratum stays within 1 point of baseline. Falsified if no K satisfies both, meaning legitimate and redundant calls are drawn from overlapping depth distributions and a scalar cap cannot separate them.

Metrics. Calls per task at p50/p95/p99, budget-exhaustion rate, accuracy by stratum, task success rate, and GPU-seconds per completed task. Guardrail: the fraction of exhausted tasks that end in a refusal or malformed answer, since a truncated agent can fail worse than a wasteful one.

Controlled experiment. Sweep K over a small pre-declared grid on a frozen checkpoint against a fixed eval set, one arm per K plus an unbudgeted control. Identical seeds and decode config; the only difference is the orchestrator constant. Record the full calls-per-task histogram per arm, not just the mean, because the intervention acts on the tail by construction.

Confounders. Task difficulty mix determines the legitimate depth distribution, so a K tuned on one traffic mix will mistune on another. Budget exhaustion changes the prompt (a new observation type the model never saw in training), which can itself degrade the final answer independently of the cap. Retries after exhaustion, if the client does them, move the cost outside the measured window.

Evidence and rollback. Calls-per-task histograms, exhaustion rates and stratified accuracy must be MEASURED per K with the eval-set id and orchestrator version. The 40% p99 reduction and 1-point accuracy band are ESTIMATE, set before the sweep as the tradeoff the operator is willing to accept. Roll back to unbudgeted if exhausted-task refusal rate exceeds 2% absolute (ESTIMATE gate); the cap is a system control and must never be reported as a model capability gain.
risks: Source proposes behavior change without any bound on call depth, leaving the tail unconstrained.
A scalar cap can truncate legitimate multi-step work if legitimate and redundant depth distributions overlap.
evidence_required: Calls-per-task histograms at p50/p95/p99 for each budget K plus an unbudgeted control.
Budget-exhaustion rate and the refusal or malformed-answer rate among exhausted tasks.

corrected_answer:
STANCE 34 - Ablate the system prompt before touching anything expensive: the cheapest sufficient intervention must be ruled in or out first.

Mechanism. Instruction-following models are strongly steerable by explicit policy statements. If the system prompt never states that tool results persist and must be reused, the policy has no textual commitment to violate. Adding one sentence is a zero-cost, instantly revertible change whose effect size bounds how much of the defect is attributable to under-specification rather than to learned habit. Failing to run this ablation first means any later training result is uninterpretable, because the training arm silently includes whatever prompt was in force.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: an explicit reuse instruction alone reduces UCR by at least 30% relative. Falsified if the reduction is under 10% relative, which would establish the defect as habit rather than under-specification and would license spending on a decode-time or training-side fix.

Metrics. UCR, accuracy by stratum, instruction-adherence rate measured by an independent judge over sampled traces, prompt token delta, and mean calls per task. Guardrail: over-correction, meaning the rate at which the model skips a call it genuinely needed after being told to reuse results.

Controlled experiment. Three arms on the same frozen checkpoint and eval set: baseline prompt, reuse-instruction prompt, and a length-matched placebo prompt that adds equivalent tokens of irrelevant text. The placebo controls for the possibility that any prompt perturbation shifts behavior, which is the standard failure of single-arm prompt studies.

Confounders. Prompt changes interact with prefix caching and can invalidate cached prefixes, changing latency and therefore any human comparison. Judge-based adherence scoring is itself a model and can be biased toward the arm whose phrasing it shares. Eval sets built from the same scenario family may reward the instruction's exact wording rather than the behavior.

Evidence and rollback. Report per-arm UCR, over-correction rate and stratified accuracy as MEASURED with the eval-set id, checkpoint hash and exact prompt texts committed to version control. The 30% and 10% bands are ESTIMATE, pre-registered as the threshold separating "ship the prompt" from "fund the training work". Revert the prompt within one deploy cycle if over-correction on the tool-required stratum exceeds 1.5 points absolute (ESTIMATE gate).
risks: Source jumps to intervention without ruling out simple prompt under-specification first.
Single-arm prompt studies without a length-matched placebo cannot separate instruction content from prompt perturbation.
evidence_required: Three-arm results for baseline, reuse-instruction and length-matched placebo prompts, with exact prompt texts committed.
Over-correction rate on the tool-required stratum and independent judge adherence scores on sampled traces.

STANCE 35 - Multi-node reality check: any arm that requires retraining must first be costed against cluster capacity and NCCL-bound scaling.

Mechanism. Proposals to fix behavior "in the weights" carry a resource claim that is usually left implicit. On a small multi-GPU node, a full fine-tune of a mid-size model is gradient-synchronization bound: every step performs an all-reduce over the full parameter set, and on PCIe-attached accelerators without GPUDirect RDMA that traffic crosses host memory. The boundary condition is the ratio of compute time per step to all-reduce time; once the latter dominates, adding GPUs buys nothing. This determines whether a training-side fix is even affordable before its efficacy is discussed.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: on the target cluster, scaling efficiency from 1 to 8 accelerators for the proposed fine-tune stays above 0.7, making the training arm affordable. Falsified if efficiency falls below 0.5, in which case the training arm is dropped in favor of a scaffold or decode-time fix regardless of its expected behavioral benefit.

Metrics. Step time at 1, 2, 4 and 8 accelerators; all-reduce time as a fraction of step time from NCCL timing; achieved bus bandwidth versus the interconnect's theoretical ceiling; tokens per second per accelerator; and peak memory per rank. Guardrail: whether the run fits without activation offload, since offload changes the scaling picture entirely.

Controlled experiment. Run a short fixed-step smoke training at each accelerator count with identical global batch size, identical data order and a fixed seed. Collect NCCL collective timings and a bandwidth benchmark on the same topology in the same session, so the interconnect measurement and the training measurement describe the same machine state.

Confounders. Topology matters more than device count: peer-to-peer availability, NUMA placement and whether GPUDirect RDMA is active can each change the result by large factors. Co-resident inference serving steals bandwidth and SM time. Short smoke runs overweight warmup and compilation cost.

Evidence and rollback. Step times, NCCL timings and achieved bandwidth must be MEASURED on the actual target hardware with driver, NCCL and framework versions recorded; nothing here may be quoted from vendor tables. The 0.7 and 0.5 efficiency bands are ESTIMATE, chosen as the affordability boundary for this cluster. Note explicitly that this analysis constrains feasibility and cost only; it is a runtime and systems result and says nothing about the model's domain capability. Abort the training arm if the smoke run cannot hold a steady step time for 100 consecutive steps.
risks: Source discusses a training-side fix with no feasibility or cost analysis on the target cluster.
Scaling and interconnect facts risk being reported as evidence about the model's domain ability rather than as system constraints.
evidence_required: Step time, NCCL collective time fraction and achieved bus bandwidth at 1, 2, 4 and 8 accelerators on the target hardware.
Peak memory per rank, driver/NCCL/framework versions, and GPUDirect RDMA status for the measured topology.

STANCE 36 - Define the labeling function before the metric: 'unnecessary' must be operationalized by a deterministic oracle or the study is unfalsifiable.

Mechanism. Every downstream number depends on a binary label that nobody has defined. "The answer is already known" can mean the value appeared verbatim in a prior observation, that it is derivable in one step from prior observations, or that the base model would have answered correctly without tools. These three definitions produce materially different rates on the same traces. Until one is fixed and implemented as code, arm comparisons are comparing labelers, not interventions.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: the three candidate labeling functions agree on at least 85% of calls, so the choice is immaterial and any one may be adopted. Falsified if pairwise agreement drops below 70%, which forces an explicit, documented choice and re-analysis of any previously reported rate.

Metrics. Pairwise agreement and Cohen's kappa between the three labelers on a stratified sample; UCR computed under each labeler; and human adjudication agreement against each labeler on a blind subsample. Guardrail: labeler runtime, since a labeler too slow to run on the full window will silently be applied to a biased subset.

Controlled experiment. Implement all three labelers as deterministic offline functions over stored trajectories. Run all three over the same frozen replay window. Draw a stratified sample of disagreement cases and have two independent human raters adjudicate blind to labeler identity, then compute kappa per labeler.

Confounders. The verbatim labeler is sensitive to formatting and will miss semantically identical values written differently. The derivability labeler needs its own arithmetic checker, which introduces a second error source. The counterfactual labeler requires extra rollouts and therefore measures a different distribution than the logged one.

Evidence and rollback. Agreement matrices, kappas and per-labeler UCR must be MEASURED on a named replay window with each labeler's code committed and versioned. The 85% and 70% bands are ESTIMATE, pre-registered as the point at which labeler choice stops being a footnote and becomes a finding. Do not report any UCR figure without naming the labeler version alongside it; any historical figure lacking that annotation must be treated as unusable rather than quietly reinterpreted.
risks: Source uses 'unnecessary call' as if it were observable, without defining a deterministic labeling function.
Rates computed under undeclared labelers are not comparable across arms or over time.
evidence_required: Pairwise agreement and kappa across the verbatim, derivability and counterfactual labelers on a stratified sample.
UCR recomputed under each labeler on the same replay window, with each labeler's code version recorded.

STANCE 37 - Disaggregated serving changes who pays: on a prefill/decode-split deployment the redundant call taxes a different pool than it appears to.

Mechanism. In a Mooncake- or Dynamo-style disaggregated deployment, prefill and decode run on separate instance pools with KV transferred between them. A redundant tool call forces the extended context back through prefill and re-establishes or migrates KV, so the marginal cost lands on the prefill pool and the transfer fabric rather than on the decode pool where user-visible tokens per second is measured. An operator watching decode-side metrics can see no degradation while the prefill pool saturates. Boundary condition: if the KV cache for the trajectory is still resident and reusable, the re-prefill collapses to a cache hit and the tax nearly vanishes.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: under disaggregation, redundant calls raise prefill-pool utilization and KV transfer volume measurably while leaving decode-pool p95 inter-token latency unchanged within noise. Falsified if decode p95 degrades proportionally, which would mean the pools are not actually isolated and the simpler colocated cost model applies.

Metrics. Prefill-pool utilization and queue depth, KV transfer bytes and transfer latency per redundant call, cache hit rate for the trajectory prefix, decode-pool p95 inter-token latency, and end-to-end p95 time to last token. Guardrail: transfer-fabric saturation, since KV movement competes with everything else on the same links.

Controlled experiment. Replay a captured window against the disaggregated deployment twice: once with redundant calls preserved and once with them elided by an orchestrator-side deduplication filter, holding the checkpoint, routing policy and pool sizes constant. The only difference is the presence of the redundant calls, so pool-level deltas are attributable to them.

Confounders. Cache hit rate depends on eviction pressure from co-resident traffic and can swing the result by an order of magnitude between quiet and busy windows. Autoscaling can mask prefill saturation by adding capacity mid-experiment. Transfer latency depends on whether GPUDirect RDMA is active on the path.

Evidence and rollback. All pool utilizations, transfer volumes and latencies must be MEASURED from the two replay runs with pool sizes, cache configuration, RDMA status and deployment versions recorded; autoscaling must be pinned for the duration. Any per-call cost figure quoted without those settings is an ESTIMATE and must be labeled as such. Roll back the deduplication filter if it changes answer content on any task, because a cost optimization that alters outputs is a correctness change wearing a performance costume.
risks: Source assumes a colocated cost model, so under disaggregated serving it attributes cost to the wrong resource pool.
Cache residency can swing the measured tax by an order of magnitude and is never recorded.
evidence_required: Prefill-pool utilization, KV transfer bytes and transfer latency with and without redundant calls on the disaggregated deployment.
Trajectory prefix cache hit rate, decode-pool p95 inter-token latency, and pool sizing with autoscaling pinned.

STANCE 38 - Pre-register the analysis: without a stated sample size, decision rule and stopping condition, whatever result appears will be the one that was looked for.

Mechanism. Redundancy rates are noisy per item and the temptation is to inspect the arms as data accumulates and stop when the gap looks convincing. That procedure inflates the false-positive rate arbitrarily. Fixing the sample size, the primary metric, the decision threshold and the stopping rule before any data is collected is what makes the eventual number interpretable. This is a methodology control, and it costs nothing but discipline.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: the pre-registered sample size is sufficient to detect the target UCR reduction at the declared power, meaning the observed confidence interval half-width comes in at or below the planned value. Falsified if the realized interval is wider than planned, in which case the run is declared underpowered and no directional claim is made rather than a weaker claim being reported.

Metrics. Primary: UCR difference between arms with a confidence interval. Secondary and explicitly labeled as secondary: accuracy by stratum, calls per task, GPU-seconds per task. Also recorded: realized sample size, number of interim looks taken, and any deviation from the registered plan.

Controlled experiment. Write the plan to version control with a commit hash before collection begins: arms, assignment rule, primary metric, target effect, sample size, decision threshold, and the stopping rule. Then collect to the planned size without interim decision-making. Paired assignment by task id keeps variance down without introducing look-ahead.

Confounders. Traffic mix drift during a long collection window changes the underlying population mid-experiment. Any unplanned deploy to either arm invalidates the comparison. Multiple secondary metrics invite selective reporting unless they are declared secondary in advance and reported in full regardless of outcome.

Evidence and rollback. The registered plan's commit hash, realized sample size, and the full metric table including all pre-declared secondaries must be published as MEASURED. The target effect size and power level are ESTIMATE, justified by what magnitude of change would actually alter the deployment decision. If the plan is deviated from for any reason, report the deviation and downgrade the result to exploratory rather than presenting it as confirmatory.
risks: Source states no sample size, decision rule or stopping condition, so any reported gap may be an artifact of optional stopping.
Undeclared secondary metrics invite selective reporting after the fact.
evidence_required: The pre-registered analysis plan's commit hash, target effect size, planned and realized sample sizes, and interim-look count.
Primary UCR difference with confidence interval plus all pre-declared secondary metrics reported in full.

corrected_answer:
STANCE 39 - Separate the two questions the scenario conflates: whether the model can abstain from calling, and whether the deployed system should let it.

Mechanism. "The model calls too often" bundles a capability claim and a policy claim. The capability question is whether the policy, given a clean prompt and a visible prior result, is able to choose not to call. The policy question is whether the operator wants that decision delegated to the model at all, given that a deterministic orchestrator-side check is cheaper and auditable. These have different evidence requirements and different failure modes, and conflating them is how scaffold wins get reported as model improvements.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: on a clean neutral scaffold with the prior result rendered plainly, the frozen checkpoint abstains correctly on at least 80% of redundant opportunities, establishing that the capability exists and the production scaffold is suppressing it. Falsified if abstention stays below 50% even on the clean scaffold, which localizes the defect in the policy and makes the orchestrator-side check the only defensible near-term fix.

Metrics. Abstention rate on redundant opportunities under the clean scaffold and under the production scaffold, with the transfer gap between them; accuracy on the tool-required stratum in both; and, for the deterministic check, its own precision and recall against the adjudicated labels. Guardrail: cases where the deterministic check suppresses a call that was genuinely needed.

Controlled experiment. Four cells: {clean scaffold, production scaffold} x {check off, check on}, same frozen checkpoint, same eval set, same seeds. The scaffold factor answers the capability question and the check factor answers the policy question; running them crossed exposes any interaction, which a pair of separate one-factor studies would miss.

Confounders. The clean scaffold is itself a design artifact and a sufficiently helpful one can leak the answer. The deterministic check's recall depends on the same normalization choices that plague the labeling function. Eval items drawn from one scenario family will not support any general capability claim.

Evidence and rollback. All four cells' abstention and accuracy figures must be MEASURED with the eval-set id, both scaffold definitions and the check's version committed. The 80% and 50% bands are ESTIMATE, pre-registered as the boundary between "unlock existing capability" and "compensate in the system". Report the check's contribution as a runtime and system result and the scaffold-gap as at most a conditional, single-family capability observation; neither may be described as a general domain-capability improvement of the model.
risks: Source conflates whether the model can abstain with whether the system should let it decide.
Scaffold-level or orchestrator-level wins can be misreported as model capability improvements.
evidence_required: Abstention rate on redundant opportunities across the crossed scaffold-by-check design, all four cells.
Precision and recall of the deterministic check against adjudicated labels, plus stratified accuracy in every cell.

STANCE 40 - Synthesis with a spend-ordered plan: each step is cheap enough to abandon, and no step may begin before its predecessor's gate passes.

Mechanism. The interventions on the table differ by three orders of magnitude in cost and revert time: a system-prompt line, an orchestrator dedup check, a decode-time constraint, and a training run. Ordering them by cost ascending, with an explicit gate after each, means the expensive arms are only ever funded by evidence the cheap arms failed to produce. The binding constraint is that each gate must be falsifiable in advance, or the ordering degenerates into doing everything.

Falsifiable hypothesis. Stated per rung. H1: the labeling function is stable enough to support any comparison (gate: pairwise labeler agreement at least 85%). H2: telemetry shows the redundancy costs enough to act on (gate: measurable spend or latency impact above a declared floor). H3: the prompt ablation alone suffices (gate: at least 30% relative UCR reduction with no over-correction). H4: an orchestrator dedup check suffices (gate: at least 60% relative reduction, precision at least 0.98 on suppression decisions). Only if H1 and H2 pass and H3 and H4 both fail does a training arm get funded, and only after the multi-node feasibility check clears. Falsified if any rung's gate passes on its own terms while the carried accuracy invariant regresses, because that would show the ladder's gates are not measuring what the deployment decision actually depends on and the whole ordering must be rebuilt around the invariant instead.

Metrics. Per rung as above, plus one invariant carried through every rung: accuracy on the tool-required stratum, which must not regress beyond 1 point absolute at any stage. Also carried: GPU-seconds per completed task and the p95 end-to-end latency.

Controlled experiment. Sequential, with each rung's arms run against the same frozen checkpoint and the same named eval set so the numbers are commensurable across rungs. Assignment paired by task id throughout. No rung starts until the prior rung's gate is evaluated and written down, including when it passes and the ladder therefore stops.

Confounders. Sequential execution spans time, so traffic drift and unrelated deploys can contaminate cross-rung comparisons unless the eval set is frozen. Passing a cheap gate creates pressure to declare victory without checking the invariant. Later rungs inherit the earlier rungs' shipped changes, so the baseline moves and must be re-measured, not assumed.

Evidence and rollback. Every gate decision must cite MEASURED numbers with the eval-set id, checkpoint hash and the code version of the labeler and any check. All thresholds named here are ESTIMATE, pre-registered as the effect sizes that would change the deployment decision on this system, not extrapolated from published results. Each rung ships behind an independently exercised revert path, and the invariant accuracy check is the single global abort criterion. Finally, record explicitly which rungs are runtime and system changes and which touch the weights, because only the latter could ever bear on model domain capability, and none of the results here establish general capability of any kind.
risks: Source presents interventions as interchangeable despite spanning orders of magnitude in cost and revert time.
Without per-rung gates, an expensive training arm can be funded on evidence that never justified it.
evidence_required: Per-rung gate decisions citing measured numbers, each with eval-set id, checkpoint hash and labeler/check code versions.
The carried invariant of tool-required-stratum accuracy at every rung, plus an exercised revert record per shipped change.
